correctness.rationale: The group-averaging reduction covers signed competing operators and preserves the quotient normalization. In 2D two explicit distance potentials yield crossing affine global lower bounds; in 3D the pair of near-midpoint potentials has opposite c-coefficient signs and eliminates arbitrary third weights, while a far-midpoint witness yields the crossing second bound. Both are exactly attained by normalized nonnegative kernels. All 2D and 3D output-pair symmetry orbits are bounded by explicit transport couplings, including the exceptional perpendicular case; radical comparisons are strict. A standard-library min-cost transport checker reproduced all 218 output pair ratios and the 3D non-distance dual witness, though numerical tests alone are not proof.

value.rationale: The unit square and cube with every edge midpoint are canonical finite interpolation/refinement configurations. The exact best simultaneous real-linear extension constants quantify stable linear sampling, and both beat arithmetic midpoint interpolation. Positive global optimizers exist despite the need to rule out signed competitors; in three dimensions the ordinary operator is dominated by a midpoint-pair interaction rather than the optimized extremal vertex-pair constraint. The specific sharp constants and coupling/dual structure are useful finite reference values, without requiring a conjectural general-dimension theorem.
